themes_detail.label: Encampment surge this week
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints in Central Harlem jumped to 17 THIS WEEK, a 249% spike from the 4.9-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks, signaling a potential sudden influx of unsheltered populations or deterioration of existing encampments that warrants urgent investigation into trigger causes and city response.
evidence: 17 encampment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (249% increase, z-score: 3.32)
Aligns with repeated CB budget requests for homeless facility upgrades, indicating chronic infrastructure gap
High statistical significance (z-score 3.32) suggests genuine operational shift, not random fluctuation
reporting_angles: Interview residents and local nonprofits to understand what triggered the sudden spike—policy change, cold weather patterns, closure of shelter beds?
Map where encampments are concentrating and identify gaps in DHS service delivery or facility capacity in CD110

themes_detail.label: Graffiti and illegal posting explosion
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked 833% to 7 THIS WEEK (vs. 0.8 weekly average) and illegal posting skyrocketed 3900% to 5 complaints LAST WEEK (vs. 0.1 weekly average), together suggesting coordinated vandalism or loss of street-maintenance enforcement control across Central Harlem.
evidence: Illegal posting: 5 complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly average (3900% increase, z-score: 14.74)
Graffiti: 7 complaints this week vs. 0.8 weekly average (833% increase, z-score: 4.81)
Both spikes emerged within the same 2-week window, suggesting coordinated or systemic enforcement failure
reporting_angles: Did DSNY reduce sanitation or enforcement patrols in CD110 recently? Request staffing changes and route data.
Interview community members about whether they've observed organized graffiti crews or increased commercial advertising violations

themes_detail.label: Vendor enforcement complaints spike
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints jumped 3100% to 8 LAST WEEK from a 0.2 weekly baseline over 8 weeks, indicating either an aggressive new enforcement sweep or sudden surge in illegal street vending that triggered community complaints.
evidence: 8 vendor enforcement complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly average (3100% increase, z-score: 11.72)
Contradicts CB's repeated budget requests to expand MWBE-owned business support—enforcement may be harming minority vendors
High z-score (11.72) confirms statistical anomaly, not noise
reporting_angles: Did NYPD or Department of Consumer Affairs launch a targeted enforcement operation? Request incident logs and vendor violation data.
Interview local street vendors and MWBE business groups: Are they being disproportionately targeted, and has enforcement changed recently?

themes_detail.label: Air quality and animal complaints emerging
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints increased 140% to 3 LAST WEEK (from 1.2 weekly average) and animal-in-park complaints surged 300% to 8 LAST WEEK (from 2.0 weekly average), suggesting potential environmental or wildlife management issues worth investigating.
evidence: Air quality: 3 complaints last week vs. 1.2 weekly average (140% increase, z-score: 4.04)
Animal in park: 8 complaints last week vs. 2.0 weekly average (300% increase, z-score: 3.46)
Both spikes emerged in same timeframe, potentially linked to seasonal or infrastructure change
reporting_angles: Did a nearby construction project (446 alteration filings in 90 days) generate dust or air quality concerns? Cross-reference DOB permits.
Contact Parks Dept about increased wildlife reports—are park maintenance cuts allowing animal populations to grow?

themes_detail.label: Water conservation complaints re-emerge
themes_detail.summary: Water conservation complaints surged 300% to 5 complaints TWO WEEKS AGO (from 1.2 weekly average), concurrent with ongoing Legionnaires' disease concerns cited in Gothamist reporting (April 7), suggesting potential water system issues affecting Central Harlem.
evidence: Water conservation: 5 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.2 weekly average (300% increase, z-score: 3.44)
Gothamist article (April 7) reported ongoing Legionnaires' disease outbreak accountability in Harlem
Underlying heat/hot water complaints (7370 over 90 days) suggest chronic water system stress
reporting_angles: Connect water conservation spike to DEP water quality advisories or boil notices issued in early April—were residents asked to conserve?
Follow up on Legionnaires' accountability story: Which buildings remain affected, and is DEP conducting new testing or corrective work?
